transcript:
Header: 2026-11-24 16:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Ana Gomez (Redwood CSM), Lena Cho (NovaPay Head of Platform), Marcus Reed (NovaPay SRE), Divya Sharma (NovaPay ML Eng), Owen Park (NovaPay Product)

Auto-summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on latency tuning. Reviewed last week's TTFT (time-to-first-token) numbers, streaming behavior, sequence length impacts, kernel selection tradeoffs, and next steps for a deeper microbenchmark (Ravi) and internal SLA confirmation (Lena). Partial transcription follows (note: ASR imperfect, some product names and acronyms may be mistranscribed).

00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we got NovaPay folks and Redwood on the line. Today the agenda is TTFT follow-up, streaming, and the kernel/quant tradeoffs we discussed last week.
00:14 Lena: Yep, thanks Sofia. We're mostly here to see the results you ran and to decide whether to push more traffi — sorry, more of our pilot into dedicated nodes or keep on hosted.
00:26 Ravi: Cool, I'll start with the numbers we collected. So last run, TTFT median was around 180ms, p95 was 360ms with streaming disabled. With streaming on we saw median 120ms but the first chunk still waits for the initial decode step so there's a slight overhead.
00:45 Marcus: Wait, when you say streaming on, are you doing chunked generation or true byte streaming? Our frontend needs the first token under 150ms to avoid spinner.
00:58 Ravi: We're doing character-chunked streaming — chunk size set to 64 tokens. There's a small batching window we allow for throughput. We can reduce the window but that increases GPU utilization and cost.
01:12 Divya: Do you have the sequence length distribution from our sample? I remember you asked for 2k and 4k mix.
01:20 Ravi: Yeah we used the 70/20/10 split you provided: 70% under 512 tokens, 20% 512-2048, 10% 2048-4096. The long tails are what's pushing the KV cache misses and kernel transitions.
01:36 Owen: Kernel transitions? You mean like different low-level kernels running depending on seq len?
01:40 Ravi: Exactly. Redwood runtime picks kernels based on sequence length and attention shape. When a lot of requests flip to long seqs mid-session it can trigger slower paths, higher memory pressure, and occasionally kernel JIT or warm-up stalls — or the ASR calls it a "kernel hitch" sometimes.
01:58 Lena: That matches what our SREs saw — sporadic spikes, not constant. We need predictability for checkout flows.
02:08 Sofia: Right, so two levers: you can cap seq_len at the model API level (truncate or offload long contexts), or we can tune the runtime: pre-warm kernels, prefer quantized kernels that are faster for long sequences, and adjust batching policies for TTFT-first.
02:28 Marcus: Can you explain TTFT-first? I want to make sure we use the right term with our infra team.
02:33 Ravi: TTFT-first is a serving mode where the runtime prioritizes generating and returning the first token as soon as possible — it can favor a small micro-batch for the initial token, then switch to larger batching for subsequent tokens. That helps UX spinner but may increase per-token cost slightly.
02:48 Marcus: Makes sense. How much cost difference are we talking about?
02:52 Sofia: Ballpark, we saw 5-12% higher token compute for aggressive TTFT-first on our 70B class models versus throughput-optimized batching. Depends on quant and hardware.
03:06 Divya: About quant — did you test int8 or 4-bit quant? Our model seems stable under 4-bit for inference.
03:12 Ravi: We ran int8 and 4-bit. 4-bit gives better memory density and often lower latency on newer kernels, but some heads/ops degrade accuracy. For your QA prompts the 4-bit topologies looked fine; we can run a focused eval. Also note kernel support varies by hardware: some older GPUs prefer int8 kernels.
03:36 Lena: From compliance POV we also need to know if KMS keys or data residency changes when we go dedicated.
03:42 Sofia: Yes, dedicated can be VPC-backed with your KMS; private plane options exist. I'll attach the security doc. We also have audit logs for request-level tracing.
03:51 Owen: Back to tuning — can you share the kernel choices you tried? We ran into a "kv cache" issue last week where session lengths blew up memory.
04:02 Ravi: Sure — we tested three kernel stacks: 1) default fused kernels (low latency for <1k seq), 2) chunked-attention kernels optimized for 2k-4k with slower startup but better steady state throughput, 3) quantized mixed kernels that reduce memory but sometimes increase single-token latency due to dequant steps. For KV issues, enabling selective KV offload to host memory for very long sessions helped avoid OOMs but hurt TTFT.
04:28 Lena: So tradeoff matrix here: TTFT vs steady throughput vs memory risk. For checkout flows we want TTFT prioritized. For batch analytics we want throughput.
04:38 Sofia: Exactly. For NovaPay's checkout, our recommendation is TTFT-first for the payment-critical route with a hard seq cap of 4096 and streaming enabled, with pre-warmed kernels and a small first-token micro-batch. For other non-critical routes you can use throughput-optimized profiles.
04:57 Marcus: What about kernel warm-up? How long does pre-warming take and does it scale with num of GPUs?
05:03 Ravi: Warm-up is typically a few hundred ms per model per instance, but we can persist warmed kernels on your dedicated pool. Cold starts happen when a model isn't pinned or after eviction. Dedicated nodes avoid evictions and keep kernels resident so warm-up is rare.
05:22 Divya: Any data on p99 improvements from pinned dedicated vs hosted?
05:27 Sofia: In our internal pilot, pinned dedicated reduced p99 variance by ~35% for long tails compared to a multi-tenant hosted pool. Absolute numbers depend on workload, but that's the trend.
05:36 Owen: Are there any quick wins we can do on our side to lower TTFT without added cost?
05:40 Ravi: Yes: a) truncate or summarize very long contexts before send, b) send only essential metadata in the first call and fetch user history lazily, c) enable streaming with small initial chunk, d) use a smaller context model for the first token then switch to a larger model if needed (model cascades).
06:02 Lena: Model cascades could be neat — start with a cheaper 13B for candidate tokens then escalate to 70B for final generation. But complexity is a consideration.
06:10 Marcus: Also our front-end can show progressive rendering if the first token is within 150ms. If you can hit that our team will be happy.
06:18 Ravi: Ok noted — our microbench will target median <120ms and p95 <250ms with streaming. We'll aim to show that with seq cap 4k and pre-warm.
06:30 Sofia: Quick aside — we noticed one transcribed term last week misread as "Redo box" — that was Redwood Dedicated. ASR keeps mangling our product names, sorry.
06:39 (laughter)
06:42 Divya: On the kernel selection, can we get the profile dump you mentioned?
06:46 Ravi: Yes I'll share the kernel timeline CSV and a short explainer. It shows per-step latency and which kernels ran for different seq ranges.
06:55 Sofia: Also we'll add notes about quant profiles that worked for your validation set. Remember that 4-bit was slightly better on our internal QA but needs your QA run.
07:06 Lena: For acceptance criteria: if we can get median <150ms and p95 <300ms for payment route under pilot load of 50rps, we'll consider moving to dedicated trial. Does that sound reasonable?
07:18 Sofia: Sounds good. We'll run benchmark at 50rps with your seq distribution.
07:23 Marcus: On security, how long do you keep logs for the pilot? We need 90 days for audit.
07:29 Ana (CSM): Our default retention on hosted is 30 days; dedicated pilot can be configured to 90 days as part of pilot contract. We'll send a formal retention option.
07:40 Lena: Great. Any blockers from Redwood side?
07:44 Ravi: The only blocker is access to your representative request traces and synthetic load script — Divya, can you share that?
07:50 Divya: Yes I'll drop in the shared drive after this.
07:54 Sofia: Perfect. Quick demo note: we'll enable TTFT-first mode for a short run and show streaming turned on. Expect an email with run artifacts.
08:05 Owen: One more question — did you see any accuracy drift when enabling streaming or quant?
08:11 Ravi: Minimal on your prompts, mainly subtle tokenization differences in rare edge cases. We'll include a diff report in the artifacts.
08:18 Marcus: Can you also include cost estimates for TTFT-first vs throughput? We need to present to finance.
08:23 Sofia: Yep I'll include the cost delta in the pricing sheet. Expect an itemized per-route estimate.
08:29 (silence / typing)
08:37 Sofia: Alright let's move to timeline and recap.
08:40 Sofia: Recap: 1) Ravi runs TTFT microbench (streaming on, seq cap 4k) and shares results by 11/30. 2) Lena confirms SLA acceptance criteria and provides internal doc by 12/02. 3) Sofia sends pricing & kernel notes by 11/26. 4) Divya to share traces and load script today.
09:05 Lena: All good. We'll aim to review results next Tuesday.
09:10 Sofia: Great thanks everyone. I'll follow up with links. Meeting adjourned.

Notes/links referenced: kernel_timeline.csv (link to shared drive), redwood-security-brief.pdf (link), pricing-sheet-novapay-v2.xlsx (link), microbench-run-artifacts/2026-11-24 (link).
